page: Microsoft Azure E4ds_v5 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the EDSv5 family. It is equipped with 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 2 physical Intel Xeon 8370C cores operating at 2.8 GHz, utilizing hyper-threading with 2 threads per core. The memory configuration provides 32.0 GB of RAM, establishing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage includes a bundled 154 GB local SSD, and the instance supports Premium Storage.

Performance benchmarks reveal a contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core execution is moderate, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores falling in the average range. However, multi-core performance is weak, as demonstrated by the stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores. Memory bandwidth tests also indicate lower-tier performance, with uncached read and write speeds categorized in the bottom 25%.

The server is configured for memory-intensive workloads that do not require dense parallel processing. The 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it suitable for relational databases, caching layers, and memory-bound data processing tasks. However, the weak multi-threaded decompression and lower memory bandwidth represent clear tradeoffs for compute-heavy applications. This profile offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring high memory capacity without the premium cost of high vCPU counts.
